items.title: Boy, 6, in coma after pool accident in Egypt to be flown back to Italy - Tajani
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, SEP 1 - A six-year-old boy who has been in a coma in an Egyptian hospital since an August 3 accident at a swimming pool at Sharm El Sheikh will be flown back to Italy in the coming hours, Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said Tuesday. The boy, Younes Majidi, suffered a cardiac arrest and has been in critical condition since nearly drowning at the Red Sea resort. Tajani said Italy never left its citizens on their own after they suffered accidents abroad. (ANSA). Read article...
items.titleIt: Boy, 6, in coma after pool accident in Egypt to be flown back to Italy - Tajani

items.description: That minister was Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur Jaamac — known in Somali political circles as Madaxa Na Furan. items.title: Energy prices push up inflation to near-three-year high of 3.3% in August (3)
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, SEP 1 - Rising energy prices due to the Iran war are continuing to push up Italian inflation, which was 3.3% in August, a near three-year high, Istat said Tuesday. According to preliminary estimates, in August 2026, the national consumer price index (NIC), excluding tobacco, will increase by +0.5% month-on-month and +3.3% year-on-year (from +2.9% the previous month). items.description: The council was briefed on Somalia's new third-generation electronic passport and was told that changes to personal data in issued passports have been stopped entirely to strengthen the document's credibility. Ministers also approved a Rules of Origin Bill allowing goods containing at least 30% Somali content to qualify for preferential treatment in regional markets. The law is aimed at boosting local production and exports following Somalia's entry into the East African Community and its participation in the African Continental Free Trade Area. items.title: AUSSOM Leadership Meets New Djibouti Ambassador to Somalia
items.description: Ambassador Diene was accompanied by Deputy SRCC Ambassador Mouktar Osman Kaire during the meeting, which focused on AUSSOM's mandate, the evolving security situation in Somalia, and recent developments related to Somali-led efforts to enhance peace, security, and stability. items.title: “Strategic Balance” under Stress: Egypt and the U.S.-Israeli War with Iran
items.description: Egypt has been walking a tightrope since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began, joining mediation efforts while signalling solidarity with Gulf Arab partners under Iranian attack. But with some Gulf capitals voicing expectations of stronger support, Cairo may find itself under increasing pressure.
items.titleIt: “Strategic Balance” under Stress: Egypt and the U.S.-Israeli War with Iran

items.description: On Wednesday, Xi Jinping and his Egyptian counterpart, president Abdel Fatah el-Sissi, oversaw the signing of a series of deals, including on technology, economic co operation and the digital economy.

items.title: US due to cut off UAE branches of Egypt's Banque Misr over Iran ties
items.description: The US Treasury Department is due to cut off a major Egyptian bank's operations in the United Arab Emirates from the US financial system, an official said Friday, as Washington pushes to choke Iran off economically.

items.title: Sudan: Sudanese Refugees Walk 20km for Aid in Eastern Chad
items.description: [Dabanga] Eastern Chad -- Dozens of Sudanese refugees have walked from Marra refugee camp in eastern Chad to the town of Amliouna to demand humanitarian assistance, as heavy rain and strong winds have also damaged shelters at Mile refugee camp near the town of Guéréda in eastern Chad.
items.titleIt: Sudan: Sudanese Refugees Walk 20km for Aid in Eastern Chad

items.title: Ethiopia: Wajirat Officials Warn of Looming Human, Livestock Deaths As Drought Devastates Southeastern Tigray
items.description: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Authorities in Wajirat district in Tigray's Southeastern Zone have warned that maximum efforts are needed to prevent potential loss of human and animal lives as a worsening drought pushes communities toward severe hunger and livestock losses.

items.title: Boy, 6, in coma after pool accident in Egypt to be flown back to Italy - Tajani
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, SEP 1 - A six-year-old boy who has been in a coma in an Egyptian hospital since an August 3 accident at a swimming pool at Sharm El Sheikh will be flown back to Italy in the coming hours, Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said Tuesday. The boy, Younes Majidi, suffered a cardiac arrest and has been in critical condition since nearly drowning at the Red Sea resort. Tajani said Italy never left its citizens on their own after they suffered accidents abroad. (ANSA). Read article...

items.title: IPI: Africa Media Freedom Monitoring: April to June 2026
items.description: The International Press Institute (IPI) recorded nearly 100 cases of threats and attacks on journalists (82 male and 18 female) across 22 countries in sub-Saharan Africa between April and June 2026. Physical and verbal attacks, as well as arrests and detention, were the most frequent types of incidents. An Ethiopian journalist in exile was found dead in Kenya under suspicious circumstances.   Police and state security forces (55%) continued to be the primary perpetrators of attacks and threats against journalists, a trend that continues from the previous quarter.
